newsitem.title: UK: UK official denies any change on EMU policy.
newsitem.headline: UK official denies any change on EMU policy.

text.p: The British government has not changed its wait-and-see policy towards a European single currency, a senior official said on Monday.

An article in the Daily Telegraph said Prime Minister John Major had the backing of 18 ministers in his 22-member cabinet for a policy shift to fight the coming general election on a pledge not to scrap the pound sterling.
But the official, an aide to Major, said: "The government will take a decision on EMU (Economic and Monetary Union) in the national interest when it is appropriate to take a decision."
He said there had been no shift in government policy since it was set out by Major himself in a newspaper article in October.
Earlier on Monday, finance minister Kenneth Clarke, widely seen as the most pro-European member of the cabinet, dismissed the Telegraph report as senseless and preposterous.

"I don't believe for one moment that anything of that kind is being contemplated," he told BBC radio. "It simply isn't going to happen. It would be senseless were it to happen." -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
